title: Prediction of Anti-Drug Antibody Risk Using a Mechanism of Action-Informed Multi-Modal AI/ML Model with MHC-II Features from Immune Epitope Database (IEDB)
content: The development of anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) represents a critical challenge in therapeutic protein development, potentially compromising drug efficacy and safety. Predicting biologically and clinically meaningful immunogenicity remains challenging with current approaches. Using data processed by AI tools from IEDB (Immune Epitope Database) to generate training data for our “homemade” machine learning model, this study explored whether mechanism of actions (immunomodulatory effects, presence of payload, solubility of target, and human similarity) plus antibody variable-region sequence features derived from MHC-peptide binding affinity, proteolytic processivity of the therapeutic antibody, and MHC-II allele population frequencies, could explain reported treatment-emergent ADA incidence. We have shown that the optimized classification AI/ML model could achieve strong performance as evidenced by standard metrics, where ROC-AUC is 0.796 and PR-AUC is 0.706, which is comparable to those of other available models for evaluating antibody immunogenicity. Therefore, sequence-derived MHC-II presentation features plus engineered MOA-related features may provide a useful starting point for developing preclinical immunogenicity risk assessment AI/ML tools.
